dataset.name: Hydrology controls thermokarst and alters carbon cycling and methane emissions in peatlands near the southern limit of permafrost: Model Inputs and Outputs
description: This dataset contains model inputs and simulation outputs associated with the study “Hydrology controls thermokarst and alters carbon cycling and methane emissions in peatlands near the southern limit of permafrost.” The ecosys model was extended to represent thermokarst processes in laterally coupled two-dimensional transects and applied to the Scotty Creek basin (Northwest Territories, Canada). The ecosys model and documentation is available for download at https://github.com/jinyun1tang/ECOSYS. The dataset contains the inputs used to run the model for this study (meteorological forcing data (1950–2018) and site-specific soil and vegetation parameters) and model outputs used to generate Figure 3 and Figure 4 in the paper (simulated ground thermal and hydrologic states, vegetation dynamics, and carbon fluxes).

measurementTechnique:
The archive includes all environmental and site-specific inputs required to drive ecosys simulations at Scotty Creek. Meteorological forcing spans 1950–2018, compiled from three sources: site tower observations (2013–2019, CA-SCC and CA-SCB AmeriFlux sites), Fort Simpson airport climate records (1963–2012), and NOAA–CIRES 20th Century Reanalysis data (1950–1963). These provide hourly time series of precipitation, temperature, humidity, radiation, and wind speed.
Soil and site property files specify bulk density, peat depth, and C/N content based on core measurements from Scotty Creek, as well as initialization of ground ice content (0.3–1.0 m³ m⁻² uniformly distributed between 1.8–6 m depth). Hydrologic boundary conditions include three prescribed external water table (EWT) positions (10 cm below surface, at surface, 10 cm above surface).
Vegetation initialization parameters are also included, with three plant functional types (PFTs: black spruce, sedges, mosses) seeded equally at the start of each simulation. PFT trait information (e.g., photosynthetic capacity, rooting depth, phenology) follows ecosys defaults and published field measurements for boreal peatlands.
Together, these forcing and input data define the site climate, soil, hydrologic, and vegetation conditions used in the transect experiments described in the manuscript.

The archive includes post-processed outputs used for analysis and Figure 3 and Figure 4 in the manuscript, including:
• Surface elevation change (subsidence from ground ice melt).
• Soil oxygen concentration (O₂).
• Tree biomass (black spruce productivity and mortality).
• Net ecosystem exchange (NEE) of CO₂.
• Methane (CH₄) emissions.
• Internal water table (IWT) depth.
